scope: Tarrant County (Fort Worth, Arlington) - healthcare, mental health, school/childcare, employment, legal, plus related local safety-net resources

records.name: MHMR Tarrant Crisis Line and Mobile Crisis Outreach
records.organization: My Health My Resources (MHMR) of Tarrant County
records.description_en: A 24-hour phone and text line for a mental health or substance use crisis. A mobile crisis team can also meet people in person in Tarrant County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Tarrant County having a mental health or substance use crisis, including children, teens, and adults.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 1-800-866-2465 any time, day or night. If someone is in danger right now, call 911. You can also call or text 988.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
records.notes: MHMR of Tarrant County is the Local Mental Health Authority for Tarrant County (confirmed on hhs.texas.gov). TTY for hearing impaired: 817-569-4488. Services include Mobile Crisis Outreach Team (MCOT), crisis residential and respite units, and the 24/7 ICARE Call Center.

records.name: MHMR Tarrant Outpatient Mental Health and Substance Use Services
records.organization: My Health My Resources (MHMR) of Tarrant County
records.description_en: Counseling, medication, and support for mental health and substance use at clinics in Fort Worth, Arlington, and North Richland Hills. There are also services for children and families.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Tarrant County children and adults who need mental health or substance use care. Fees are based on a sliding scale.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-335-3022 to start services. Adult new-patient intake is held at each center on set days, for example the South Center (1200 Circle Drive, Fort Worth) on Monday and Friday 8 a.m.-2 p.m.
records.hours: Adult new-patient intake 8 a.m.-2 p.m. on set days by center: South (1200 Circle Dr, Fort Worth) Mon & Fri; Central (300 Pennsylvania Ave, Fort Worth) Tue & Fri; East (601 W. Sanford Suite 11, Arlington) Mon & Fri; West (6777 Camp Bowie Blvd Suite 600, Fort Worth) Thu & Fri; North (4525 City Point Dr, North Richland Hills) Wed & Fri
records.notes: Also offers child and family centers, Early Childhood Intervention (ECI), IDD services, and veteran services. Call first to confirm whether intake is walk-in or by appointment at a given center. For families with children 0-6: Help Me Grow North Texas 844-689-5437.

records.name: JPS Connection
records.organization: JPS Health Network (Tarrant County Hospital District)
records.description_en: A discount health care plan for Tarrant County residents. Members can see JPS doctors and specialists and get low-cost prescriptions.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Tarrant County residents with household income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents and must first apply for any other health coverage they may qualify for.
documents_needed: Picture ID for all applicants (government, school, or work ID)
Birth certificates for all child dependents
Proof of income for all household members (pay stubs, award letters, etc.)
Agency award letters (SNAP, TANF, Housing, CHIP/Medicaid, SSI, etc.) if any
Bank statements for last 30 days (if homeowner, self-employed, or on Social Security)
Proof of homelessness if applicable (shelter letter or agency letter)
Signed Form 4506-C and Membership Responsibility Form
records.how_to_apply: Apply online, or drop off your application and documents at a JPS Enrollment & Eligibility Center. You can also email, fax, or mail it. Call 817-702-1001 for help.
records.notes: Plan levels: Connection 1 (under 21% FPL), Connection 2 (below 100% FPL), Connection 3 (101-250% FPL), plus supplemental plans for people with Medicare or insurance below 250% FPL. Email enroll@jpshealth.org; fax 817-702-3834. Main hospital: 1500 S. Main St, Fort Worth (817-702-3431).

records.name: Northside Community Health Center
records.organization: North Texas Area Community Health Center, Inc. (NTACHC)
records.description_en: A community health center (FQHC) with family, women's, children's, and behavioral health care. Fees are on a sliding scale by income and family size.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, including people without insurance. Staff can help you apply for Medicaid, CHIP, or Marketplace insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-625-4254 to make an appointment. Ask for a financial assessment to get the sliding fee.
records.hours: Mon-Thu 7:20 AM - 7:00 PM; Fri 7:20 AM - 6:30 PM
records.notes: Federally Qualified Health Center. Sliding fee info confirmed at https://ntachc.org/financial-assistance/.

records.name: Southeast Community Health Center
records.organization: North Texas Area Community Health Center, Inc. (NTACHC)
records.description_en: A community health center (FQHC) in southeast Fort Worth for adults and children. Fees are on a sliding scale by income and family size.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, including people without insurance. Staff can help you apply for Medicaid, CHIP, or Marketplace insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-625-4254 to make an appointment. Ask for a financial assessment to get the sliding fee.
records.notes: Federally Qualified Health Center.

records.name: Arlington Community Health Center
records.organization: North Texas Area Community Health Center, Inc. (NTACHC)
records.description_en: A community health center (FQHC) in Arlington for adults and children. Fees are on a sliding scale by income and family size.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, including people without insurance. Staff can help you apply for Medicaid, CHIP, or Marketplace insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-625-4254 to make an appointment. Ask for a financial assessment to get the sliding fee.
records.notes: Federally Qualified Health Center.

records.name: Bob Mann Medical Clinic
records.description_en: A free medical clinic for low-income people. It gives basic care, sample medicines, and help getting prescriptions.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of Arlington, the Tarrant County part of Grand Prairie, Kennedale, Mansfield, Pantego, and Dalworthington Gardens.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Arlington, Tarrant County part of Grand Prairie, Kennedale, Mansfield, Pantego, or Dalworthington Gardens

records.how_to_apply: Go to the clinic at the Mission Arlington main offices. Patients are seen first come, first served.
records.hours: 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Monday-Friday; 6:00 p.m. Tuesdays; first come, first served
records.notes: Located at Mission Arlington main offices; street address was not shown on the page read. Main Mission Arlington line: 817-277-6620.

records.name: Allan Saxe Dental Clinic
records.description_en: A free dental clinic run by Mission Arlington.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in need in the Arlington area. Call for details on who can be seen.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-860-4474 for a new appointment.
records.notes: Mission Arlington states there is no charge for any service provided.

records.name: Mission Arlington Counseling Services
records.description_en: Free counseling services offered by Mission Arlington.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in need in the Arlington area.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-704-6144 to ask about counseling.

records.name: Mission Arlington Emergency Assistance
records.description_en: Free emergency help such as food, clothing, and help with basic needs. All services are free.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in need in the Arlington area.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-277-6620 or visit during emergency assistance hours.
records.hours: Emergency Assistance: Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturday 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
records.notes: Page did not detail the exact types of emergency aid (for example rent/utility amounts); call to confirm what is available.

records.name: Cook Children's Neighborhood Health Center - Arlington
records.description_en: A pediatric clinic for children from birth through the teen years. Staff speak English and Spanish.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children and teens. The clinic accepts Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-804-1100 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance accepted
records.notes: Page did not state a sliding fee or uninsured policy.

records.name: Cook Children's Neighborhood Health Center - Renaissance
records.description_en: A pediatric clinic in southeast Fort Worth for children from birth through the teen years, with evening hours. Staff speak English and Spanish.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children and teens. The clinic accepts Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-347-4600 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance accepted
records.notes: Other Fort Worth sites: Northside (4405 River Oaks Blvd, 817-624-1770), Miller (2755 Miller Ave, 817-534-7110), McCart (6421 McCart Ave, 817-263-7500), Las Vegas Trail (2800 S. Cherry Ln Suite 100, 682-303-2800), Manhattan (6825 Manhattan Blvd Suite 106, 682-303-6825), Morris Foundation Center (1729 8th Ave, 682-885-3301).

records.name: Cook Children's Neighborhood Health Center - Northside
records.description_en: A pediatric clinic in north Fort Worth for children from birth through the teen years, with evening hours. Staff speak English and Spanish.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children and teens. The clinic accepts Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-624-1770 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Medicaid, CHIP, and most commercial insurance accepted

records.name: Tarrant County Public Health Clinical Services
records.description_en: The county health department offers immunizations, tuberculosis care, HIV/STI testing, and maternal and child health services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Tarrant County residents. Call to ask about costs and requirements for each service.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-884-1111 to ask about a service and where to go.
records.notes: Costs per service not stated on the page read.

records.name: Tarrant County WIC Program
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy food, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support to pregnant women, new moms, babies, and young children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 who meet WIC income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-321-5400 to schedule a WIC appointment at your local WIC clinic.
records.hours: Clinics: Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-1 p.m. and 2-6 p.m., plus one Saturday a month. Appointment line: Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-6 p.m.
records.notes: Address shown is the Southside clinic. Other clinics: Bagsby-Williams (3212 Miller Ave, FW 76119), Eastside (1100 Bridgewood Dr #116, FW 76112), Lake Worth (3800 Adam Grubb, FW 76135), Resource Connection (2500 Circle Dr Suite 400, FW 76119), Southwest (6551 Granbury Rd, FW 76133), White Settlement (1638 S. Cherry Ln, FW 76108), Arkansas (2596 E. Arkansas Ln, Arlington 76014), Green Oaks (2001 S.E. Green Oaks Blvd, Arlington 76018), Haltom City (4113 Denton Hwy, 76117). Application info: https://www.tarrantcountytx.gov/en/public-health/family-health-services/wic-program/how-do-i-become-a-wic-client-.html

records.name: Workforce Solutions for Tarrant County - Job Seeker Services
records.description_en: Free help finding a job, including resume review, interview practice, job fairs, workshops, and career training. Services are in person and online.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in Tarrant County. Some training programs have extra requirements.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a Workforce Center or call 817-413-4000. You can also start online at the website.
records.notes: TDD/TTY 1-800-735-2989. Center names include Arlington, Central, Resource Connection, and Mid-Cities Workforce Centers. Fort Worth address confirmed on the Texas Child Care Connection listing (https://www.childcare.texas.gov/taxonomy/term/331); check the locations page for current center hours and any closures.

records.name: Arlington Workforce Center
records.description_en: A job center in Arlington with free job search help, career training, and workshops.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center or call 817-413-4000.
records.notes: Main line 817-413-4000 is from the Workforce Solutions homepage; TDD/TTY 1-800-735-2989.

records.name: Child Care Services (CCS) Scholarships - Tarrant County CCMS
records.organization: Child Care Associates, for Workforce Solutions for Tarrant County
records.description_en: Helps pay for child care so parents can work, look for work, or go to school or training. Most families pay a share of the cost based on income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Texas families with a child under 13 (or under 19 with a disability) who is a U.S. citizen or has legal immigration status. Parents must meet work, school, or training and income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply on the Texas child care portal, or call 817-831-0374 for help.
records.cost: Parent share of cost based on income
records.notes: The CCMS site says there is currently a CCS waitlist in Tarrant County. Income limits and parent share chart: https://www.childcare.texas.gov/for-families/child-care-scholarships. Children up to 19 qualify if they have a disability. Program support email: programsupport@tarrantcountyccms.org.

records.name: Early Head Start / Head Start Early Learning
records.description_en: Early childhood education for children 6 weeks to 5 years old, with family support for money, health, and nutrition. It is free for eligible families.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families with young children (6 weeks to 5 years) who meet program rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-484-1545 or email EarlyLearning@TransformingLives.org to ask about enrolling.
records.notes: Centers are throughout Tarrant County and on Fort Worth ISD campuses, plus a UTA campus site at 1120 UTA Blvd, Arlington 76013. Specific income rules were not listed on the page read.

records.name: Rent and Utility Assistance (Tarrant County Community Outreach Fund)
records.description_en: Short-term help paying rent and/or utility bills for Tarrant County residents. Tarrant County moved its rent and utility help to this agency in November 2025.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Tarrant County residents who need short-term help with rent or utilities. Call for income and other rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 607-8137 or visit the Get Help page to start.
records.notes: Tarrant County Human Services lists (817) 607-8137 and Communityoutreach@transforminglives.org; the Center for Transforming Lives general line is (817) 332-6191. Eligibility and documents were not listed on either page read.

records.name: Community Action Partners (CAP) Utility Assistance and Case Management
records.organization: City of Fort Worth Neighborhood Services - Community Action Partners
records.description_en: Help paying electric, gas, and propane bills, plus HVAC repair, home safety repairs, and case management. This is the Community Action Agency for Tarrant County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Tarrant County residents with low income. Some veteran programs are only for Fort Worth residents.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online when the portal opens (9 a.m. every other Friday) or book an in-person appointment. Call 817-392-2276 if you do not have internet.
records.notes: Local CEAP provider for Tarrant County. The online portal closes each week once the maximum number of applications is reached; the page listed openings through September 2026, so check for the new schedule. A 'Documents Required' PDF is linked on the page. Due to high demand, calls may not be answered right away.

records.name: Tarrant Area Food Bank - Find Food
records.description_en: The regional food bank helps you find a nearby food pantry or mobile pantry. It also helps people apply for food benefits like SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone who needs food in Tarrant County and nearby counties. Each pantry may have its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food map on the website to find a pantry near you, or call 817-857-7100.
records.hours: Monday - Thursday 8:30 a.m. - 5 p.m.; Friday 8:30 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. (main office)
records.notes: The main office is a warehouse/office, not a walk-in pantry. SNAP application help: https://tafb.org/apply-for-food-benefits/

records.name: Trinity Metro Reduced Fare
records.description_en: Lower bus and train fares in the Fort Worth area for seniors, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, youth, and veterans. A local single ride is $1 and a 1-day pass is $2.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Seniors 65+, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, youth ages 5-19, and veterans with proof of status.
documents_needed: Valid ID showing age (Texas ID, driver's license, Medicare card, or birth certificate) for seniors
For disability: Medicare card, Social Security award letter, or VA benefits award letter, plus photo ID
records.how_to_apply: Show valid ID when buying a reduced ticket. People with disabilities can get a reduced fare photo ID at Fort Worth Central Station, 1001 Jones Street.
records.cost: Reduced fare: $1 local single ride, $2 1-day pass, $9 7-day pass
records.notes: No income-based low-income fare was listed on the page read.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - Fort Worth Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, including evictions, tenant problems, foreclosure, family law, debt, and more.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income individuals and families in its 114-county service area, which includes Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Call the intake line at 1-888-529-5277 or apply online.
records.notes: Handles housing, eviction, foreclosure, homelessness, landlord-tenant, family law, custody/support, debt collection, immigration. Exact income limits not stated on the page read. If facing an eviction hearing, apply as early as possible.

records.name: Catholic Charities Fort Worth
records.organization: Catholic Charities Diocese of Fort Worth
records.description_en: Case management and services such as immigration legal help, refugee services, low-cost dental care, transportation, financial coaching, and job help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in the 28-county Diocese of Fort Worth. You do not need to be Catholic.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-534-0814 or use the Get Help page on the website.
records.cost: Varies by service; dental care is low-cost
records.notes: Pregnancy and parenting line: 1-800-545-5935. Email: infocatholiccharities@ccdofw.org. Rent/utility help was not listed on the page read.

records.name: The Archway (formerly SafeHaven of Tarrant County)
records.description_en: 24/7 crisis help, safety planning, shelter and housing, support for children, and legal services for survivors of domestic violence.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of intimate partner violence in Tarrant County and nearby areas.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at 1-877-701-7233 for help or shelter.
records.notes: Office line for the Arlington location: (817) 535-6462. Shelter locations are kept confidential; use the hotline. The old safehaventc.org site redirects here.

records.name: Presbyterian Night Shelter Emergency Shelter
records.description_en: Emergency shelter open 24/7 with beds, meals, case management, and help finding housing and work.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone experiencing homelessness.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the shelter at 2400 Cypress St. or call 817-632-7400.
records.notes: Also runs UpSpire, a social enterprise that offers jobs to people with barriers to work.

records.name: True Worth Place Day Shelter
records.description_en: A daytime resource center for people experiencing homelessness. It has showers, laundry, lunch, a mailing address, phones, computers, case management, and job programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone experiencing homelessness, whether staying in a shelter or on the street.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in during open hours.
records.hours: 7 days a week, 365 days a year, 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

records.name: Arlington Life Shelter
records.description_en: Shelter, meals, case management, job programs, and transitional services for people experiencing homelessness.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness in North Texas.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 548-9885 to ask about intake.
records.notes: Intake hours not listed on the page read; call first.

records.name: Fort Worth Housing Solutions
records.description_en: The Fort Worth housing authority. It runs Housing Choice Vouchers, affordable housing, homelessness programs, and family self-sufficiency programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income households. Waitlists open only for certain properties.
records.how_to_apply: Check which waitlists are open and apply through the online portal, or call 817-333-3400.
records.notes: At time of research only a property-specific waitlist (Sedona Village Senior Living PBV) was shown as open. Texas Relay 7-1-1 for hearing impaired.

records.name: Arlington Housing Authority
records.organization: City of Arlington - Arlington Housing Authority
records.description_en: Runs the Housing Choice Voucher program, home repair help for homeowners, and a family self-sufficiency program in Arlington.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low and very low-income households, seniors, and people with disabilities in Arlington.
records.how_to_apply: The voucher waiting list is closed right now. Call 817-275-3351 to ask about home repair or other programs.
records.notes: Page says the Housing Choice Voucher waiting list is closed and is not expected to reopen due to funding levels.

records.name: Tarrant County Veteran Services
records.description_en: Free help for veterans and survivors to apply for VA and Texas veteran benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Veterans and their survivors.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-531-5645 for an appointment, or come in for limited walk-in service Tuesday-Friday. Fill out the New Client Intake form.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-3 p.m. by appointment; Tue-Fri 9 a.m.-3 p.m. limited walk-in; closed 12-1 p.m. daily
records.notes: Email: VeteranServices@tarrantcountytx.gov

records.name: Recovery Resource Council
records.description_en: Substance use screening, outpatient treatment, recovery support, and counseling for individuals, couples, families, and children. Free mental health services for veterans and their families.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in its 61-county North Texas, West Texas, and Panhandle service area, which includes Fort Worth. Telehealth is available.
records.how_to_apply: Call 817-332-6329 to ask about services.
records.cost: Free for veterans' mental health services; other costs not stated
records.notes: Fort Worth street address not shown on homepage.
